Writing it now.

action_items.item: Roll out io-shop feature flag changes to a small share of traffic first, and roll them back automatically if the error rate rises.
Run io-shop's test suite in CI with each feature flag in both states, so a code path a flag opens is tested before the flag can be changed.
Review whether the HighErrorRate rule on io-shop can fire with a shorter hold without becoming noisy.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so a person is paged when it fires.
Lock legacy-checkout-fallback ON against further changes until the fix in PR #569 is merged.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the account page error rate rose far above its usual level.
The account page requests failed because rendering them raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors first appear in the onset minute.

ruled_out.what: A deployment: when the change events were read, no deploys came back for the window read before the onset.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus in the {T15.3} hour before {T15.4}, and that change was this one.

causal_chain.step: The division by zero began when admin switched the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback off at {P1.1}. Before that, every evaluation read the flag as on and account pages rendered normally. Evaluations started reading off in the minute of the change and read off in every minute after it.

With the flag off, account pages likely take the monthly spend-summary path, which divides by the number of items bought this month, and that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: An administrator switched off a feature setting, which sent account pages through a monthly spending summary that likely breaks, by dividing by zero, for any shopper who has bought before but nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag change reached all of io-shop's traffic within the minute it was made. No staged rollout and no check before the change was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout with a check on the error rate would have shown the failures on a small share of requests and stopped the change before it reached most shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that runs the account page with legacy-checkout-fallback off for a shopper who has past purchases but none this month. Code-Fix's new tests for that case raise against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero on the monthly path would have been caught before the path was ever turned on in production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate rule waits {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires, so the error rate stayed high for some time before anything acted on it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: With a shorter hold, the alert, and so the flag revert, would have come sooner, and the incident would have been shorter.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: Argus called in the Investigator Agent as soon as it took up the alert.
The Investigator Agent formed candidate C1, which tied the failures to the flag change.
The Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback back to ON.
The Mitigation Agent judged the revert CONFIRMED once the service was no longer at the incident's level.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request PR #569 for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was brought in to respond.

input.root_cause: With legacy-checkout-fallback off, account pages take the monthly spend-summary path. There, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`, and nothing guards against that number being zero. So for any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError, which `render_spend_summary` passes up to `serve_account_page`, and the page is recorded as failed.
input.still_at_risk: If legacy-checkout-fallback is switched off again, account pages can fail again for shoppers who have past purchases but none this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed to load for many shoppers
